editorial:
Imagine waking up to a loud bang that only you can hear. That is exactly what happens to Jessica, a Scottish woman visiting Colombia. You will find yourself following her as she tries to figure out why she keeps hearing these strange sounds. The whole movie feels like a dream where time slows down. It is not a loud or flashy film, but it draws you in with its quiet mood and beautiful shots of nature. You get to feel her confusion and curiosity as she searches for the source of the noise.

The acting is very natural, making you feel like you are just hanging out with Jessica. Be warned that the pacing is very slow, so you need to be in a patient mood. If you like stories that make you think and feel instead of just giving you answers, you will love this. Since the sound is such a huge part of the story, you should definitely watch it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or rent it on Apple TV to get the best audio experience. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move.
endingExplained: In the end, Jessica meets a man who can help her hear the sounds better. He uses a special tool to connect her to the past. You see that Jessica is not just hearing a noise, but memories from thousands of years ago. The movie ends with her finally connecting with the history of the earth. She finds a sense of peace knowing she is part of a much bigger story that spans across time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves artistic stories and doesn't mind a slow pace.
